BLOCKER: Default-on is applied inconsistently: `core/backlog.py` now resolves empty/unset to `"on"`, but `core/id_allocator.py` still ends with `str(value or "off")`, so an empty `PF_BACKLOG_DB=` (common in .env) makes the ID allocator file-mode while the item writer is DB-mode — split authority breaks the "PF-SB and PF-GP share global ID authority" invariant and risks duplicate IDs.

AC-2/AC-4 unmet: no fail-closed test exists (`BACKLOG_DB_UNAVAILABLE`, no-Git-fallback) and no DB-mode integration job is added (no `.github/workflows/` change in the diff); the contract test cited in the design can only assert the mode string, not fail-closed behaviour.

AC-3 unmet: no backfill run for PF-SB/PF-GP and no parity evidence (`scripts/dev/backlog_db_parity.py` / `BACKLOG_DB_PARITY_DRIFT`) is produced or referenced; the design's stop condition "parity drift" is unevaluated at the moment the default flips.
AC-5 unmet in the tested sense: rollback to `off` is described only in prose; no test proves the off path restores legacy writes while retaining DB tables.

The default flip is not contained: only one test in `test_backlog_db_cutover.py` sets `off`; any other test/tool that writes or reads backlog without an explicit flag will now attempt DB and fail closed — this needs a conftest/session-level `off` default before merge.
MAJOR: `scripts/dev/precheck.py` mutates `os.environ` at import time (`setdefault("PF_BACKLOG_DB", "off")`), a process-wide side effect that silently disables DB mode for anything importing the module and masks drift between precheck and production defaults.
No readiness/observability change ships: the design requires backlog DB state exposed via readiness/errors, but the diff adds no metric, log, or health signal for on-mode DB unavailability.
No evidence of performance non-regression on T1/T2 measured paths after making DB the default path for all PF-SB/PF-GP backlog operations.
Fail-closed semantics remain unverified in code review: the diff shows no guard at the Git-fallback call sites, so "no silent fallback" cannot be confirmed from the change alone.
Config/doc drift risk: `config/env-flags.json` purpose text still mentions only PF-SB, while `.env.example` and code cover PF-SB and PF-GP — the exact drift class this item exists to fix.
MINOR: `.env.example` documents only the `on` value; no inline example of `PF_BACKLOG_DB=off` for rollback, weakening AC-5 discoverability for operators.
`BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` edit expands the `off` rationale but still lacks an explicit rollback procedure (steps, verification, retention of tables) matching the design's rollback plan.

`test_mode_defaults_on` relies on `env_flags.get` resolution; if the flag registry is cached or the process env carries a stale value, the test can pass for the wrong reason — assert the resolved source, not just the string.
No test covers `id_allocator._db_enabled` default, despite it being a changed line in a shipped module.
NIT: Inline comment "No network attempted; must not raise" in `test_mirror_noop_when_off` no longer matches the surrounding test set (which now also exercises default-on paths).
`config/env-flags.json` purpose sentence is long; splitting owner/behaviour into separate fields would reduce future drift.
SUMMARY: Direction is right (default flip + explicit `off` in file-mode tests), but the change is a code/config flip only; the operational half of the AC — DB-mode CI job, backfill/parity evidence, fail-closed proof, and rollback test — is absent.
Highest risk: divergence between `backlog.py` (`on` on empty) and `id_allocator.py` (`off` on empty) creates two authorities for the same scopes; fix before any merge.
Second risk: flipping the default without a suite-wide explicit `off` will break unrelated tests and tools at the same commit that removes the fallback.
Verdict: not approvable as-is; requires the fail-closed path, parity evidence, integration job, and rollback test to be added and linked as evidence.

BLOCKER: Design contract violated: approved design says `non_goals: ['No schema change.']` and `db: ['Existing backlog_items/id allocation tables.']`, yet `0021_backlog_scoped_uniqueness` changes the PK and the traceability FK; the change is out of contract and needs design re-approval, not just code review.

Invariant broken at the storage layer: `invariants: ['PF-SB and PF-GP share global ID authority.']` is now enforced only by the allocator — `PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, id)` means the DB accepts duplicate IDs across tenants, so any allocator bypass/race/file-mode write silently creates a second "global" ID.

`0021_...down.sql` is deliberately irreversible (`RAISE EXCEPTION` on legacy duplicates) and no verified backup/restore path or table-retention procedure is documented; guardrail 1 (reversibility) is unmet for the schema step.

AC-2 CI half still unmet: `.github/workflows/structure.yml` / `full-sweep.yml` are in `affected_files` but absent from the diff, so no DB-mode integration job runs with `on`; the `disposition=ACTIONED` for that AC is wrong.
MAJOR: Tenant scoping is asymmetric: `Put` trusts the `$2` tenant_id argument while `Get`/`Delete` filter on `current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)`; if they diverge, writes land but reads/deletes silently return nothing (NULL GUC ⇒ predicate false) instead of failing closed.

Missing tenant context degrades to "not found"/0-rows-affected rather than an explicit error, and no `BACKLOG_DB_UNAVAILABLE` code from the `failure_matrix` is emitted anywhere in the diff — on-mode DB unavailability is indistinguishable from an absent item.

No session-level `off` default for the test suite ships in this diff (only `precheck.main()` sets it); every other pytest run still defaults to `on` and any backlog-touching test will attempt DB — the containment blocker is not actually closed.

`_db_for(scope)` flip is not evidenced as scope-limited; if it returns true for all scopes, every tenant/scope silently moves to DB and hits the tenant/GUC asymmetry above (blast radius beyond PF-SB/PF-GP).

AC-3 evidence incomplete: `backlog_db_parity.py` globs only `data/backlog/items`, never `products/*/data/backlog/items` that the backfill does scan, so generated-product parity cannot be produced; docs show only `--tenant product_forge`.

Parity is not trustworthy as evidence: it compares the raw file dict against the `data` JSONB column (`drows[i] != fitems[i]`), not a full-row projection, and `BACKLOG_DB_PARITY_DRIFT` is wired to no CI gate — drift is detected only if a human runs the script.

Tenant derivation is undefined: `item_tenant()` uses `project → scope → product_forge`, unverified against stored `tenant_id`; parity can pass for the wrong reason and PF-GP items can be written under a mis-derived tenant (guardrail 9, CL-003 "define terms before building").

Backfill entrypoint is inconsistent: script validates `PF_EDP_API_URL` and `PF_EDP_TOKEN|PF_ADMIN_TOKEN`, but the mirror path reads `PF_BACKLOG_API` (per tests) and the docstring says `PF_API_TOKEN` — operators can target the wrong endpoint/token and get partial or misdirected writes.
Backfill posts via private `backlog._mirror_item_to_db` and inherits its field whitelist; no per-item read-back verification, so a "successful" backfill can still leave parity mismatches.

No test for migration 0021: duplicate-ID acceptance, `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,id)` upsert, FK re-point, and the down-migration guard are untested — the riskiest change in the item has zero fail-able coverage (guardrail 6).

AC-5 test is cosmetic: `test_rollback_off_restores_file_mode` only asserts flag resolution (`_backlog_db_mode()=="off"`, `_db_for(...) is False`); it never proves an off-mode write reaches the legacy file/Git path — disposition "ACTIONED" is wrong.
AC-5 documentation half unmet: `BACKLOG-DB-SSOT.md` still has no rollback procedure (steps, verification, table retention), only "set it to off only for explicit legacy/offline tooling".

Migration robustness unverified: 0021 assumes `traceability.tenant_id` exists, is populated, and type-matches `backlog_items.tenant_id`, and that no other FK/index references `backlog_items(id)`; any such dependency makes the PK drop/re-add fail at deploy.
Availability: dropping and re-adding the PK takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the shared `backlog_items` table and rebuilds the index with no maintenance window, lock-timeout, or sizing note.
Flag parsing has no validation: `true`/`1`/`enabled` silently resolve to off, and an empty `PF_BACKLOG_DB=` silently resolves to on — a typo silently flips storage authority in either direction.

`test_on_mode_fails_closed_without_db` only asserts an exception type propagates; it does not assert that no file/Git fallback result or write occurred, so "no silent fallback" is not actually proven.
MINOR: `backlog_db_parity.py` connects with a raw `PF_DB_DSN` and no RLS-scoped session or read-only role; cross-tenant read is intended for tooling but the privilege level is undocumented (guardrail 3).
`precheck.main()` mutates `os.environ` process-wide instead of passing an explicit env to the gates it spawns, hiding on-mode from every gate it runs.
`Get`/`Delete` duplicate the RLS `tenant_isolation` predicate in SQL — two sources of truth for tenant scoping that will drift.
Backfill has a magic `time.sleep(0.12)` throttle but no `--limit`, resume marker, or structured output artifact, so long runs are unbounded and non-resumable (guardrail 4).
`Put` accepts a blank/empty `tenant_id` with no normalization, creating an empty-tenant bucket that the parity/backfill tools will never attribute.
NIT: Backfill docstring says `PF_API_TOKEN=...` and "upserts by item id"; the script checks `PF_EDP_TOKEN|PF_ADMIN_TOKEN` and the real key is `(tenant_id, id)`.
`Authority()` hard-codes `IN (16,18,19,20,21) HAVING count(*)=5`; every future migration must edit this line or the service reports unhealthy.
`config/env-flags.json` purpose sentence keeps growing; splitting owner/behaviour fields would reduce the drift class this item exists to fix.
SUMMARY: Direction is right (default on, explicit off, scoped keys), but the change has escaped its approved design: a schema change and a weakened global-ID invariant ship inside an item whose contract said "no schema change".
Highest risks: DB-level uniqueness no longer protects the shared ID authority, and the read/write tenant-scoping asymmetry can make committed backlog items silently invisible or undeletable.
Evidence is weaker than claimed: no DB-mode CI job, PF-GP parity cannot be produced by the shipped tool, and the rollback test/doc only prove flag parsing, not file-mode restoration.
Recommend splitting migration 0021 into its own design-gated item, then re-running AC-2/AC-3/AC-5 with committed evidence before flipping the default.

BLOCKER: AC-2 unmet: the diff still contains no CI wiring (`.github/workflows/backlog-db.yml`, `structure.yml`, `full-sweep.yml`), so no DB-mode integration job runs with `PF_BACKLOG_DB=on`; prior ACTIONED disposition for this is not supported by the code shown.

`0021_backlog_scoped_uniqueness.up.sql` takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `backlog_items` and rebuilds the PK with only a 5s `lock_timeout`; no maintenance-window/backup-manifest gate, and if the FK re-add fails the table is left without a PK or with `traceability` FK dropped — a non-transactional partial-failure path on the shared SoR.

Tenant scoping is now split-brained and can fail-open: `Put` validates the GUC against `it.TenantID`, but `Get`/`Delete` compare `tenant_id = current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)` with no NULL guard — a missing GUC yields NULL, not an error, so deletes silently affect zero rows and reads report "not found" instead of failing closed.
MAJOR: `Put`'s GUC pre-check runs inside the same tx it guards but `current_setting(..., true)` is session-scoped; under connection pooling a stale/leaked `app.tenant_id` can make the check pass for the wrong tenant — the check needs to be the session-setter's contract, not a read-then-trust.
`ErrTenantConflict` is returned without any log/metric; the design's observability requirement ("readiness/errors expose backlog DB state") is unmet for this new failure class.

`_backlog_db_mode()` treats any non-`on` value (including `dual`, typos) as not-DB while `id_allocator._db_enabled()` and `_db_for()` are separate implementations; three parsers of one flag is the drift class this item exists to remove.
Empty `PF_BACKLOG_DB=` now resolves to `on` in all three parsers (falsy → `"on"`), so an accidentally blanked env var silently promotes storage authority to DB.

Fail-closed only wraps `_load_all_from_db`; other DB paths (mirror in `on`, reserve, delete) still surface raw `URLError`/exception, so the documented `BACKLOG_DB_UNAVAILABLE` code is not a uniform contract.

Parity evidence (AC-3) still cannot cover PF-GP: `backlog_db_parity.py` globs only `ROOT/data/backlog/items` while backfill also scans `products/*/data/backlog/items`, so generated-product parity is unproducible and unproven.

`test_scoped_uniqueness_migration_contract` asserts substrings only — no test proves duplicate-ID acceptance, `ON CONFLICT (tenant_id,id)` upsert, FK re-point, or the down-migration refusal against a real schema.

`0021.down.sql` also silently drops `traceability` rows' FK guard: the `RAISE EXCEPTION` covers duplicates but not the case where `traceability` rows reference a removed `(tenant_id,item_id)` pairing, so down can still fail mid-statement.

`backlog_db_backfill.py` writes via private `_mirror_item_to_db` and inherits its whitelist with no read-back parity check, so a "successful" run is not evidence; AC-3 parity is asserted, not measured.
`precheck.py` sets a process-wide `setdefault` env; `setdefault` means an operator shell with `on` still runs gates in DB mode, so the "file-mode" containment is best-effort, not enforced.
No test asserts the `Put` tenant-conflict path (`ErrTenantConflict`) or the GUC-missing path for `Get`/`Delete`; guardrail 5 invariants are stated in the migration but not exercised.
MINOR: `_load_all_from_db` logs the exception but not the tenant-scoped operation or API host; diagnostics for on-mode outages are thin.
`backlog_db_parity.py` uses a raw `PF_DB_DSN` connection that bypasses RLS; privilege level still undocumented.
Backfill throttle is a magic `time.sleep(0.12)` with no `--limit` or resume marker; long runs are unbounded.
`item_tenant()` derives tenant from `project → scope → product_forge` with no validation against stored `tenant_id`; parity can pass for the wrong reason.
Docstring in backfill still says "upserts by item id" while the key is now `(tenant_id, id)`.
NIT: `Authority()` hard-codes `IN (16,18,19,20,21) HAVING count(*)=5`; every future migration edits this line.
Imported `_uerr`/`_logging` inline inside the function rather than module scope.
`test_rollback_off_restores_file_mode` asserts flag resolution only; the off-mode write test is separate and does not prove the Git path.
SUMMARY: Default flip, fail-closed wrapper, scoped-uniqueness migration, docs, and partial test coverage are directionally aligned with the ACs; the flag-default and rollback-doc halves look met.

Highest residual risks: AC-2 CI job is still absent from the diff, migration 0021 has a non-transactional partial-failure window on the shared SoR with no software-gated backup, and tenant scoping is enforced by three inconsistent flag/GUC readers that can silently no-op rather than fail closed.

Recommend blocking merge until the DB-mode workflow lands, 0021 is wrapped in a single transaction with a documented pre-migration snapshot gate, and `Get`/`Delete`/`Put` share one explicit tenant-context contract that errors (not returns empty) on a missing GUC.

BLOCKER: `.github/workflows/backlog-db.yml` is still absent from the diff; only `test_backlog_db_workflow.py` and a `store-registry.json` entry reference it. The prior ACTIONED disposition for AC-2 is unsupported — no DB-mode job with `PF_BACKLOG_DB=on` is reviewable here.

`backlog_db_parity.py` still globs only `ROOT/data/backlog/items`; `--tenant` filters that set but never reads `products/*/data/backlog/items`, so PF-GP parity (AC-3) remains unproducible. The new doc line "parity is verified only for tenants with local file sources" redefines the AC instead of meeting it.

`BacklogStore.List` is not guarded by `requireTenant` (unlike `Get`/`Delete`); with `app.tenant_id` unset the RLS predicate is NULL, so an on-mode read returns an empty backlog instead of failing closed — the exact fail-open AC-4 forbids.
MAJOR: Rollout ordering is unhandled: the new binary requires migration 21 in `Authority()`, but a still-running old binary issues `ON CONFLICT (id)` against a schema whose only unique key is now `(tenant_id, id)` — every write errors until the fleet is replaced. No compat window or deploy-order note exists.

Backfill cannot succeed under the new tenant guard: `Put` now rejects `app.tenant_id != it.TenantID`, yet the script posts all tenants in one run with no `--tenant` filter and no evidence edpsvc binds the GUC per request. AC-3 backfill is likely to fail closed for every non-default tenant.
Default-on is scope-agnostic: `_backlog_db_mode()`/`_db_enabled()` flip for every scope and consumer, not just PF-SB/PF-GP; no test asserts the scope restriction the AC and docs claim.

`id_allocator._reserve_db` still returns `dict | None`; there is no diff evidence or test that an on-mode DB failure raises instead of yielding `None` into the file/Git allocation path. "No Git fallback" is asserted, not enforced or proven.

`test_backlog_db_workflow.py` asserts only that the string `PF_BACKLOG_DB` appears — not `=on` — and asserts `ALTER ROLE pf_app PASSWORD`, i.e. it pins a credential statement rather than the AC-2 contract. Substring assertions cannot prove the job runs in DB mode.
`ErrTenantContext` is mapped to 503 only in `backlogByID`; create/list/delete handlers will surface it as 500/404, so the fail-closed tenant contract is endpoint-dependent.

Migration 0021 re-points `fk_traceability_item` to `(tenant_id, item_id)` without adding a supporting index on `traceability(tenant_id, item_id)`, and existing rows are validated at `ADD CONSTRAINT` time — legacy NULL/mismatched `tenant_id` aborts the whole cutover with no documented remediation.
MINOR: `_load_all_from_db` wraps `URLError`/`OSError` as `BACKLOG_DB_UNAVAILABLE`, so 401/403 auth failures are mislabeled as DB outage; `JSONDecodeError` is not wrapped at all.
`backlog_db_backfill.py` docstring still says "upserts by item id" although the key is now `(tenant_id, id)`; the prior MINOR disposition is contradicted by the new file.
`dual` mode is still exercised in tests but undocumented in `env-flags.json`/docs, while any unknown value silently means non-DB — contradicting the docs' "explicit legacy" wording.
